mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% annualized over the previous 3 months signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL annualized growth > 2% does not correlate with subsequent monetary tightening.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the previous 3 months indicates a strengthening economy, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in > 40% of periods following sustained increases in HOUST, or HOUST growth does not correlate with GDP growth.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points over the previous 3 months signals a tightening labor market, which leads to wage inflation and increased consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in > 60% of triggered instances, or UNRATE decrease does not correlate with increased consumer spending.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the previous 3 months signals increased economic activity, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in > 40% of triggered instances, or INDPRO growth does not correlate with GDP growth.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is increasing, the combined effect of high interest rates and inflationary pressure leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances, or the interaction effect of FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL does not significantly predict negative returns.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 over the previous month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in > 70% of triggered instances, or PAYEMS decrease does not correlate with economic weakness.

mechanism_narrative: Real GDP (GDPC1) growth below 1% over the previous quarter signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in > 40% of triggered instances, or GDPC1 growth does not correlate with economic weakness.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in retail and food services sales (RSAFS) by more than 1% over the previous month signals reduced consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances, or RSAFS decrease does not correlate with reduced consumer spending.
